plan: My goal is to maximize profit. Given my value is $30, I want to win if the second-highest bid is less than $30. I will bid slightly below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Since bids are in $0.1 increments, I will bid $29.9 to maximize my profit while still having a high chance of winning against other bidders who might bid closer to their values.

My value is $7. Since this is the first and only round, I need to maximize profit for this single round. The optimal strategy in a second-price auction is to bid my true value. This ensures I win if I'm the highest and my value exceeds the second-highest bid, maximizing my profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value, while bidding lower risks losing a profitable opportunity.

Given this is a first-price sealed-bid auction with payment equal to the second-highest bid, it's a Vickrey auction variant. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes your utility regardless of other players' bids. My value is $36. I will bid my true value.
